column2: text
Welcome! Care to buy something to eat?
Come, come, young one! Buy some weapons! Mine are the finest!
Welcome, welcome! Buy some armor to protect yourself!
Sorry! That number is not right!
Too much! You can't carry any more!
Maiyin Corridor
This month has been terrible: the earth shook, thunder and rain without end. They say beastmen from Mount Wuta were seen in town, and someone was even attacked.

Legend says the sun god Saiou loves to ride the wind to the far north, and each time he decks his wind chariot with ten thousand purple-heart flowers. That is why the purple lights of the north are called the "purple solar wind".
Sangdesi, don't wander out of the village. If you must go, take a weapon to defend yourself. They say many beastmen have gathered outside the village, and they hurt people.
I hear the legendary mage-priests all have undying souls, so even when they die they can come back to life.
Sangdesi, your father is truly great! If King Maiya had not called on him, no one would have known he was a knight of the Wall Knights, the strongest order in the world!
Sangdesi, your father must have left some fine weapons at home. Why not go home and look?
Legend tells of a book called the Heaven's Notes, full of prophecies. They say whoever gets it gains tremendous power.
Huh! What are you carrying that worn-out badge for? It won't keep the beastmen off.
Your father is the Wall Knight who saved the Bangpei Empire! Our king asked him to search for the lost Princess Daini. Didn't you know?
Some say that in the siege of the Bangpei Empire twenty years ago, King Sigao and Queen Ailun fought on, twenty against a hundred thousand, and then were luckily carried off by a thick fog.
Your father left in a hurry. He asked me to tell you he left some things in the cellar at home. I think you'd better go and look.
I hear that past the Maiyin Corridor, if you keep going north, you will find Mount Qichong.

Don't go near the beastmen outside the village; they're terrifying! Some look like crabs, some have three heads, and there are green monsters sticky all over. You can drive them off with exorcism shots.
The old folks say the Demonstar Charm can call up the seven great mages who died. Use four Demonstar Charms, and Nadi, the most terrible of them, the Archmage, will rise again.
Uncle Siteli is telling stories at his house again. Want to listen? He lives in the second house from the village gate.
I don't know what's got into Uncle Siteli; he keeps telling the same story. I've no wish to hear it again.
All quiet in the village lately.
In a moment I'm going east of the village to pick tata fruit for Uncle Siteli. Want to come?!
I hear Dazhou went through many hardships before he found the entrance to the underworld.
You will surely succeed!
They say Mount Qichong has a seven-colored bird that got wisdom and magic from Mount Mata, so many people want to try their luck at Mount Mata. Sigh... without strength you can't take a single step.
Dazhou was swallowed by a fire dragon on his way to Wugeer, the underground kingdom. Sigh! The entrance to the underworld is a mystery again.
So glad to see you!
If you want to hear a story, you should know the rules here!
Come in!

Long ago on the planet Hongqi, the lands were joined as one, the seas flowed around them, and its civilization was the finest in the Great Red Galaxy. But in the year 1682 of the Ya Era, a strange thing happened in the Bangpei Empire: at the
first-birthday feast of the young prince Hudu, a horn grew from his forehead before hundreds of guests. To hide the rumor that the queen might have lain with a beastman, the once-kind King Kaluoan I
had every guest in the hall put to death. Afterwards Nadi, the Archmage who served the king, led the ten strongest mages and the beastmen of Mount Wuta and, in the name of

vengeance, marched against the king. On the fifth day the king and queen took their own lives together, but that did not stop Nadi; her cruelty only grew. Not content with slaughtering people, she used sorcery and
super-science to overturn the world. In the end Nadi was sealed away by five godlike warriors. The tale of the horn was told and retold until it became an unsolved mystery.
A painting signed Sangdesi. A line beside it reads: "Painted by Sangdesi, age nine."
Sangdesi: If you are reading this letter, something must have happened. Whatever happens, listen to your father: put your own safety first in everything, and never go
wandering about looking for me. There are fifty gold coins in the chest; use them to buy food until I return. Finally, I must tell you that I am really a Wall Knight. The Wall Knights were the
strongest guard of the Bangpei Empire's last king, every one a brave warrior. So trust me: before long I will settle this and come home safely.\n                       - Your father, Sangruike
